title: Effect of research paper mills enough to start affecting LLM query results
key_facts: Anton Sokolov, doctoral student at Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) and researcher at the Tyche Institute, studies retractions of bogus science.
Retraction Watch lists about 61,000 retracted papers from 2010 to 2025, about two per thousand papers a year.
His dataset of nearly 15,000 retraction records in computer science: authorship violations under 2%; peer-review problems cited in about 7 of 10 notices; computer-generated text about one third.
A Novaator experiment in early September bought co-authorship for $800 in 20 days.
In a study published last year, a language model did not mention the retraction in more than 6,500 assessments of retracted or questionable papers.
His preliminary pilot calculation: more than 20,000 papers flagged by the Problematic Paper Screener had not been retracted as of June.
He suggests authors digitally sign their contributions.
quote_evidence: The number of retractions shows how much is being cleaned up, not how much garbage remains.
The risk is real and it has already been measured.
At the moment, an author of a scientific paper is simply a name in the text.
why_it_matters_hint: If flawed papers enter model training data, chatbot answers could repeat them.
event_date: Interview published around 4 Oct 2026; Novaator experiment early Sep 2026
notes: One researcher's views and a preliminary calculation; reported by ERR as an interview. Kept at 5.
